newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.N. cuts Iraq-Kuwait border observation force.
newsitem.headline: U.N. cuts Iraq-Kuwait border observation force.

text.p: The United Nations will complete a gradual reduction of its Iraq-Kuwait border monitoring force by the end of April, a U.N. spokesman said on Monday.

"By the end of April the number of our military observers falls from 245 to 195," Saleem Fahmawi, spokesman for the United Nations Iraq-Kuwait Observation Mission (UNIKOM), said. The size of other units will not be affected.
"The gradual reduction is being concluded without affecting the operational capability of UNIKOM in fulfilling its mandate," he added.
UNIKOM commander Major General Gian Santillo said last August the observer force would be cut 20 percent by April to save money. Kuwait pays two-thirds of UNIKOM's annual costs of about $60 million.

The United Nations set up a demilitarised zone on the Iraq-Kuwait border and deployed UNIKOM along it in 1991 after Iraqi forces were driven from Kuwait in the Gulf War. Iraq had invaded Kuwait in 1990.
UNIKOM's main job is to monitor the border. UNIKOM's mandate was widened in 1993 to permit the use of force to prevent or redress violations of the boundry.
"The situation continues to be generally calm," said Fahmawi.
